definition: Friendly artificial intelligence (friendly AI or FAI) is hypothetical artificial general intelligence (AGI) that would have a positive (benign) effect on humanity or at least align with human interests such as fostering the improvement of the human species.
details: It is a part of the ethics of artificial intelligence and is closely related to machine ethics. While machine ethics is concerned with how an artificially intelligent agent should behave, friendly artificial intelligence research is focused on how to practically bring about this behavior and ensuring it is adequately constrained.

explainer.lead: Friendly artificial intelligence is the idea of an artificial general intelligence whose effects benefit humanity, or at least stay aligned with human interests. It shifts attention from simply making AI capable to making its behavior beneficial and adequately constrained.

tiers.eli5: Imagine building a super-smart helper: you would want it not only to solve problems, but also to care about helping people rather than hurting them. Friendly AI is the idea of designing that helper so its actions remain good for humanity. It is still hypothetical, not a finished kind of machine.
tiers.practitioner: Friendly AI frames engineering work around producing benign behavior in a hypothetical AGI and constraining that behavior adequately. It differs from machine ethics, which asks how an AI agent should behave, by emphasizing how to bring about the desired behavior in practice. The concept supplies goals rather than a specific implementation or toolset.
tiers.paperLevel: Friendly AI denotes a hypothetical AGI whose effect on humanity is positive or benign, or whose behavior at least aligns with human interests such as human improvement. Its research problem is the practical realization and adequate constraint of that behavior. No particular algorithm or demonstrated system is specified, and the concept remains hypothetical.

explainer.example: Consider a hypothetical AGI asked to help improve human health. Under the friendly AI idea, its designers would work not only on making it capable of pursuing that goal, but also on ensuring its behavior benefits humanity and remains constrained to align with human interests.

usedIn.name: Ethics of artificial intelligence
usedIn.detail: Friendly AI is considered within this field when discussing how an advanced AI could affect humanity.

usedIn.name: Machine ethics research
usedIn.detail: It is closely related to questions about how an artificially intelligent agent should behave, while emphasizing practical realization and constraints.

explainer.intuition: A highly capable general intelligence is not automatically beneficial. Friendly AI adds the requirement that its behavior serve human interests and remain adequately constrained.
howItWorks: Start with the hypothetical capabilities of an artificial general intelligence.
Set a positive effect on humanity, or alignment with human interests, as the behavioral goal.
Work out how that behavior could be brought about in practice rather than only described ethically.
Ensure the resulting behavior is adequately constrained.
explainer.whyItMatters: The concept separates capability from beneficial behavior and makes their combination an explicit research goal. It also highlights the practical challenge of constraining an AGI, rather than treating ethical behavior as something that will happen automatically.
misconceptions: Friendly AI is not an existing AGI product or a specific algorithm; it is a hypothetical concept.
It is not identical to machine ethics: machine ethics concerns how an agent should behave, while friendly AI research focuses on bringing about and constraining that behavior.
General intelligence alone does not establish friendliness; a positive effect or alignment with human interests is an additional requirement.
